header: Date: 2027-06-09 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 55m | Recording: yes | Location: Zoom
summary: Weekly POC sync focusing on persistent latency spikes at tail, access gap for staging VPC, and next remediation steps. SE confirmed a KV-cache warmup issue plus a missing TLS SNI config on Bluewave side causing occasional 502s. Action items agreed around KV cache tuning, firewall changes, and a short benchmark run after fixes.
topics: Access & gateway certs (VPC peering, firewall rules)
KV cache warm-up and batching configs
Security: KMS, audit logs, SOC2 scope
transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Park: ok, thanks everyone for joining, um, we'll try to keep this to about 45 minutes but we have 55 on the calendar so, you know, wiggle room. Quick intros?
[00:12] Maya Singh: Maya here, ML eng, hi.
[00:15] Carlos Ortega: Carlos, platform./ sorry had a late build break.
[00:18] Diego Morales: Diego, se on Redwood side, focusing on infra and latency today.
[00:22] Priya Reddy: Priya, CTO.
[00:24] Anika Bose: Anika, CSM.
[00:28] Jamie Park: Cool, agenda — 1) recap of last week's bench, 2) tail-latency deep dive, 3) access issues and certs, 4) next steps. Any critical additions?
[00:36] Maya Singh: No, that's about it. We also want to re-validate encryption at rest for the staging dataset.
[00:40] Jamie Park: noted, Ellen from security can jump in on that later.
[00:45] Diego Morales: I'll kick off the latency stuff — summary first: we see steady median at ~80ms on the 8k prompt set but p95 jumps to 430 and p99 is 820ms in a few bursts; the initial assumption was batching related but traces show a KV-cache miss pattern.
[01:03] Carlos Ortega: Is that the KV cache on Redwood's side or our prefix cache?
[01:07] Diego Morales: Redwood's runtime maintains an LRU KV cache for session tokens and prefix reuse — but you can have warmup issues if there's a lot of cold-started contexts, and we saw heavy context-switching in your test harness.
[01:20] Maya Singh: Right, our test harness spins up ephemeral sessions per request which was to emulate mobile clients, maybe that's too synthetic.
[01:26] Diego Morales: Yep that explains misses. We also caught a config mismatch — your gateway wasn't passing the SNI header consistently so occasionally requests dropped to fallback path — fights with TLS renegotiation caused the 502 spikes.
[01:40] Priya Reddy: So two parallel causes — warming and TLS. Which is higher priority?
[01:44] Diego Morales: TLS fixes are quick — firewall and SNI change on your side. KV tuning needs a bench run post-change.
[01:50] Jamie Park: I'll put firewall and cert steps in the action items. Carlos can you confirm who owns the LB config?
[01:55] Carlos Ortega: I'll take it, that's on platform. We use an internal LB that terminates TLS and healthchecks to 10.0.5.23, I think SNI was stripped by the ingress for some routes.
[02:05] Ellen Zhao: On the security note: we need to confirm KMS integration for key rotation, plus retention windows for audit logs — SOC2 scope items. We can't ship pilot logs outside the approved bucket without encryption policy.
[02:15] Anika Bose: Redwood can provide audit log exports and a KMS integration guide — Jamie will send the doc.
[02:21] Jamie Park: Yup, sending SOC2 summary + KMS steps after this call.
[02:24] Diego Morales: Back to KV: our recommendation is to tune max_cache_entries and batch_timeout from defaults; for your workload I prototyped increasing cache from 64k entries to 256k and raising continuous-batch window slightly to 12ms. That should cut tail by about 20-30% in lab sims.
[02:41] Maya Singh: 12ms window vs default? we had it at 5ms previously to prioritize latency.
[02:45] Diego Morales: Right, median may increase a touch but p99 improves; it's a cost-latency trade. We can try an adaptive policy too.
[02:52] Priya Reddy: We care more about p99 for end-user experience, so leaning to p99 reduction.
[02:57] Jamie Park: Good note. We'll run a controlled bench with both configs and share CSVs. Diego, how long will the bench take?
[03:02] Diego Morales: 2 hours for a thorough run including warmup and steady-state tails, then another hour to parse graphs. So about 3 hours.
[03:08] Carlos Ortega: Do you need us to reconfigure load generation so sessions reuse cookies?
[03:12] Diego Morales: Please — if you can send a variant of the harness that reuses a session cookie across N requests that will show warm vs cold behavior.
[03:17] Maya Singh: Will do. We'll also include 16k prompt shapes for high-token scenarios.
[03:21] Jamie Park: Great. Next, access: Carlos, you mentioned earlier the ingress strips SNI for internal healthcheck routes, is that actionable?
[03:28] Carlos Ortega: Yes, it's a small config flag on the ingress controller, we'll flip it for the pilot routes. We will confirm cert chain and SNI propagation by Monday.
[03:35] Diego Morales: Also, there's a TLS ciphers policy mismatch — older client cipher negotiated and triggered extra CPU on our side for decrypts; that's why some requests spiked. We recommended TLS1.2+ modern ciphers; if your LB can force ciphers that would reduce CPU overhead.
[03:50] Ellen Zhao: We have a conservative cipher baseline but can loosen for pilot endpoints inside the VPC; will coordinate with Carlos.
[03:55] Priya Reddy: What about data residency — we need to ensure the staging logs stay in the EU region.
[03:59] Jamie Park: Noted — we support regional endpoints and will ensure logs written to EU bucket only for the pilot. I'll document that in the SOW.
[04:07] Maya Singh: On cost — curious if increasing cache size will elevate memory on the instances and impact dedicated vs hosted decisions.
[04:12] Diego Morales: Yes marginal RAM goes up; it's small relative to a GPU instance. If you're on Dedicated it's trivial to increase, for Hosted we can change quantization profile and memory usage is still manageable.
[04:22] Jamie Park: If Bluewave picks dedicated pool later, we can size GPUs accordingly. For now the pilot can run on hosted with tuned cache.
[04:29] Carlos Ortega: One other hiccup — our CI bot was flooding the staging env with parallel requests which made the bench noisy last week. We'll gate that.
[04:36] Jamie Park: Good, please block non-bench traffic during the test window.
[04:40] Diego Morales: Ok, technical proposal: 1) Carlos flips SNI/pass-through & cipher policy (done before bench), 2) Bluewave re-run harness with session reuse and 16k prompts, 3) Redwood runs 3-hour bench (warmup + steady state) and shares p50/p95/p99 CSV + flamegraphs, 4) iterate on cache/batch settings.
[04:58] Maya Singh: Sounds good. For bench windows, mornings are better for us (UTC mornings).
[05:02] Jamie Park: We'll propose two slots in Monday-Tuesday morning UTC.
[05:05] Anika Bose: Regarding pricing — Jamie will re-send pilot pricing and a lean SOW that enumerates effort and deliverables for KV tuning, bench runs, and 2 weeks of post-run monitoring.
[05:15] Priya Reddy: Want to make sure SLA language around fallback is explicit; if the host path degrades, how fast can you roll to a fallback model?
[05:21] Diego Morales: We support automated fallback to smaller model variants at the routing layer; typical failover is seconds but depends on KV cache priming. We'll include a failover playbook in the SOW.
[05:33] Jamie Park: Ellen — any open security blockers?
[05:35] Ellen Zhao: Need the KMS integration design and a sample audit log format. Also a short pen-test scope for pilot endpoints. We won't sign off without those.
[05:44] Jamie Park: We'll deliver KMS steps and sample audit log by Friday. Also propose a brief pentest scope doc.
[05:49] Maya Singh: One practical ask — can you annotate the CSV with which runs were cold vs warm? That will help us interpret p99 delta.
[05:55] Diego Morales: Yes will add a "warmstart" column, and include HTTP trace ids to correlate 502s to cert issues.
[06:02] Carlos Ortega: I'll open a ticket with our LB config change and paste logs after flipping SNI.
[06:07] Jamie Park: Ok let's recap actions and owners.
[06:10] Diego Morales: Diego — run bench and produce flamegraphs (due 2027-06-16).
[06:14] Maya Singh: Maya — provide revised harness with session reuse and 16k prompts (due 2027-06-11).
[06:18] Carlos Ortega: Carlos — flip ingress SNI & cipher policy and validate cert chain (due 2027-06-14).
[06:22] Jamie Park: Jamie — SOC2/KMS notes, pricing and SOW (due 2027-06-12).
[06:28] Anika Bose: I'll coordinate scheduling and send potential bench slots.
[06:31] Priya Reddy: Great, thanks, appreciate concise next steps.
[06:34] Jamie Park: Any final Qs?
[06:36] Maya Singh: None from me.
[06:37] Ellen Zhao: No.
[06:39] Jamie Park: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts. Meeting adjourned.
